Source: EM Guidance EMCT Snakebite Emergencies, accessed 
24/10/2024 

 
ABORT SEIZURE 
FIRST LINE AGENTS - BENZODIAZEPINE 
0.3 mg/kg buccal / intranasal 
 
** If the seizure continues, administer a 2nd dose of the chosen benzodiazepine 
• Phenytoin 
20 mg/kg IV 
(max rate 50 mg/min) 
• Sodium Valproate 
20 - 30 mg/kg IV 
(max rate 3-6 mg/kg/min) 
• Phenobarbitone 
20 mg/kg IV 
LOAD WITH A 2nd 
LINE 
ANTICONVULSANT 
STATUS EPILEPTICUS 
ANTICONVULSANT ALGORITHM 
 
 
 
 
 
• Lorazepam (Ativan) 
0.1 mg/kg IV 
(max rate 2mg/min) 
• Diazepam (Valium) 
0.2 – 0.3 mg/kg IV 
(max rate 5mg/min) 
• Clonazepam (Rivotril) 
0.02 mg/kg IV 
• Midazolam (Dormicum) 
0.2 mg/kg IV 
 
 
 
 
 
 
IF SEIZURE CONTINUES 
 
IF SEIZURE TERMINATES 
 
LOAD WITH A SECOND LINE ANTICONVULSANT 
 
IF SEIZURE CONTINUES 
 
REPEAT 2ND LINE ANTICONVULSANT after 20 minutes 
 
• 
Phenytoin 
10 mg/kg IV 
(max rate 50 mg/min) 
• 
Sodium Valproate 
10 mg/kg IV 
(max rate 3-6 mg/kg/min) 
• 
Phenobarbitone 
10 mg/kg 
 
IF SEIZURE CONTINUES 
 
 
REFRACTORY STATUS EPILEPTICUS 
THIRD LINE ANTICONVULSANT 
• Midazolam (Dormicum) 
Loading Dose 0.2 mg/kg IV then 
Infusion 
0.1 mg/kg/hr (0.05 - 2mg/kg/hr) 
• Propofol 
Loading dose 3 – 5 mg/kg IV then 
Infusion 
1 – 15 mg/kg/hr 
• Ketamine 
Loading dose 1.5 mg/kg then 
Infusion 
0.01 – 0.05 mg/kg/hr 
 

 
 
STATUS EPILEPTICUS 
 
Immediate Management 
• 
ABCD approach to initial resuscitation 
• 
Don’t ever forget glucose 
• 
Hypoglycaemia 
1ml/kg of 50% Dextrose IV 
5ml/kg 10% Dextrose IV (child) 
if no IV line – 50% dextrose buccal 1ml in children; 2-5mls adults 
 
Airway and Breathing 
• 
Patient position – lateral 
• 
Supplemental oxygen (nasal prongs/FMO2) 
• 
Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI) if seizures continue for 
 5 minutes (see RSI protocol) 
 
Circulation 
• 
Insert an IV line 
• 
Shock: Fluid bolus 20ml/kg of Balsol/Ringers Lactate 
 
Drugs 
• 
Glucose if hypoglycaemia 
• 
Benzodiazepine to abort seizure 
• 
Load with 2nd line anticonvulsant agent 
• 
See status epilepticus anticonvulsant algorithm 
 
 
PRECIPITATING FACTORS 
• 
Infection / Intoxication 
• 
Metabolic / Electrolyte abnormalities (HypoNa) 
• 
Trauma / Toxins (INH, TCA) 
• 
Drug toxicity (anti-epileptics) 
• 
Eclampsia, thyrotoxicosis 
• 
Intracranial haemorrhage / ischaemic stroke 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
History 
• 
Detailed history of seizure 
• 
Identify precipitating factors 
 
Physical Examination 
• 
Vital signs 
• 
General examination & any evidence underlying diseases 
• 
Neurological examination 
• 
Signs of meningitis 
• 
Focal neurological deficit 
 
Investigations 
• 
ECG, blood glucose and blood gas on ALL patients 
• 
Urine-HCG on ALL female patients 
• 
Tailor further investigations to clinical findings 
• 
Urgent CT brain with contrast if: 
• 
No return to baseline 
• 
Focal neurological deficit 
Identify and treat the precipitating factor 
Disposition 
• 
Consult Neurology/IM as appropriate 
DEFINITIONS 
Status Epilepticus 
Continuous seizures for 5 minutes or  2 discrete seizures in close 
succession without full recovery of consciousness between episodes 
Refractory Status Epilepticus 
Seizures persisting despite  2 anticonvulsant agents (i.e. 
1st & 2nd line anticonvulsants)
